message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to say "See you next year!" to this teacher who's getting let go. Let me start by understanding the situation better. First, there's this teacher, R, who was new at my school this year. From the start, he tried to impose his own way of teaching and grading, which was very different from what we, the students, had ever experienced. It sounds like he was pretty rigid about things, expecting everyone to do things his way, even if it wasn't the best approach. People pointed out that his methods were flawed, but he still insisted on using them. That's frustrating because it shows a lack of willingness to adapt or consider others' perspectives. Additionally, R took points off for scratch work that he didn't like, and he tried to deduct as many points as possible on tests, quizzes, and homework. Every student he had was subjected to this, without exception. That's really harsh and doesn't seem fair. It creates a stressful environment for the students, especially if they're being penalized for things that aren't directly related to their understanding of the subject. R also took forever to grade assignments. We took a test the week before spring break and didn't get it back for about six weeks. That's a long time, and it means students can't learn from their mistakes in a timely manner. It also shows a lack of commitment to his teaching responsibilities. Moreover, R refused to go over the test with anyone, which is another missed opportunity for students to understand where they went wrong and how to improve. He also never offered help outside of the classroom and was hostile whenever asked for extra help. This makes him seem unapproachable and unwilling to support his students, which is a big problem for a teacher. The administration noticed these issues, and we were informed that R wasn't coming back next year. It's no surprise that we were overjoyed about this news. After the announcement, R completely checked out. He wrote notes on the board, barely talked during class, and even went to Disneyland instead of attending one of the review days for exams. This behavior shows a lack of responsibility and commitment to his students, especially at the end of the year when review is crucial. Yesterday, as I was walking out of R's classroom for the last time, I called out, "See you next year!" over my shoulder. My friends told me I'm the asshole for this, but I don't think so. I'm trying to figure out if I was right or wrong to say that. So, why did I say that? Well, I was probably reacting to the frustration and relief I felt about R not being our teacher next year. It was a way to express that we were glad he wasn't coming back. But my friends think it was mean or inappropriate. Maybe they feel that it was disrespectful to the teacher, even though he wasn't the best. I need to consider a few things here. First, was my intention to be disrespectful, or was it more about expressing my feelings? Second, how did R react to it? Did it cause any harm or further issues? Third, is there a better way to express those feelings without being disrespectful? I also need to think about the broader context. Teachers are professionals, and even if they're not performing well, they deserve respect. Saying something like "See you next year!" when they're being let go could be seen as mocking their situation, especially if they're already feeling down about it. On the other hand, I was just expressing my feelings about the situation. It's natural to feel relieved when someone who's been causing stress is leaving. But the way I expressed it might have come off as unkind or insensitive. Maybe I should have found a more constructive way to handle my emotions. Instead of making a comment that could be seen as disrespectful, I could have focused on the positive aspects of moving on and not engaging in negative behavior. In the end, I think it's important to balance expressing my feelings with maintaining respect for others, even if they're not performing well in their role. It's a tough line to walk, but being mindful of how my actions and words affect others is crucial.
